chapter: Radio, Jazz Record and Blue Note (Reel 2)
title: The Jazz Record magazine: Cow Cow Davenport and 60 issues
summary: The Jazz Record ran 60 issues from February 1943 to November 1947. It published musicians' stories word for word, and Hodes calls Cow Cow Davenport's piece priceless.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: No, I think he might have contributed. But that was not the name. But in any case, we got beautiful pictures, we got stories, priceless stories. Cow Cow Davenport's story to me is priceless. He never wrote another thing in his life.
Told it to us like I'm telling you. It was word for word.
Typed as fast as he wrote. We had no other way of doing it.
If there was any words. But with Cow Cow don't think there was any words. It was very simple. He didn't use --
And, of course, this magazine is The Jazz Record.
Jazz Record, which now became the book, Selections From the Gutter. But this was it. And we kept that going for 60 issues, over four years.
And when did you start it, '42?
We started in -- I think the first one was February, '43. And it lasted through November, '47.
Whose idea was it for the title, Jazz Record?
